As of today: (1) **Phase T's rendered-extent deltas** — point size held, extent moves, T81 ruled that IS the measurement and `TvTypeParityProbe.cs` reports it rather than tuning it; (2) **T78-am's base-instance question**, plus the width-axis fingerprint routed from T82 (bounded there — advance alone cannot separate weight from width, and which asset `cb84278` loaded decides what the ratio means); (3) **T82's digit-width deltas** on every figure slot of every rebuilt asset; (4) **any G1 overrun** surfaced by G1-am2, carried as a span-or-size question. Anything joining later joins by amendment, named **T74-am2 · batch 42 — the magnitudes ruled, with their levers.** **`RiskPays` 16.1 px over today, 39.8 px under tabular.** **An exemption will be proposed and the argument is better than it looks:** the mandate's stated mechanism is *change in place / twitch on every tick*, and **RISK and PAYS do not tick** — both are fixed the moment the ticket is placed, the cash-out figure being the one that moves; under **C40's** proxy-versus-property distinction (*"money"* is the proxy, *changes in place* the property) a static money figure has no twitch to prevent, and it gains no column alignment either since RISK and PAYS sit side by side rather than stacked. **REFUSED anyway, and NOT on that reasoning — the exemption is unavailable BY CONSTRUCTION:** T75-am fixed the unit at the **font asset** and T82 confirmed the fix is cmap-only per asset, so since **`RiskPays` and `CashOut` are both condensed Bold 700 — one asset — and the cash-out figure ticks**, exempting RiskPays needs a SECOND condensed Bold asset for one slot, the shape refused three times (S70's fourth ground for one string, T77's second family for one slot, R41's second model). **Ruled: RiskPays takes tabular because its ASSET-MATE needs it** — the reasoning is recorded because it is sound and will recur, and the next person to raise it deserves to be told it is right about the mechanism and defeated by the asset. **Lever: span then size, never the copy** (§4 / T24-am); the value is T74's on its own frames, under this seat's constraint that **the ticket column's outer width does not move** (T46, R30) — relief comes from inside the row. **`LegRowLine0` passes by 3.4 px today and FAILS by 1.8 px on wiring** — the smallest number in the docket and the one that gates the wiring commit (T82-d). **The dead-backstop box and the wiring casualty are the SAME box:** with the backstop dead an overrun here would have shipped silently, and TV fixing it and re-measuring through the live measurer converts a silent defect into a loud one, which is the right direction. **But a working backstop is a DETECTOR, not a REMEDY — C40 again:** *truncation fires* is the proxy, *the string fits* is the property, and **G1's entire charter is that truncation is never reached** — so a LegRowLine0 truncating on the wiring commit is a violation that announces itself, not one that has been handled, and nobody may read "the backstop works now" as closure. **Ruled: 1.8 px of relief lands BEFORE wiring.** **`MARKET SUSPENDED`** routing unchanged from T84-am — span first by prior ruling (TV-12/13 grants it the slot exclusively); its number joins T74's table when it arrives. **THE INVENTORY IS SIX SLOTS SHORT AND SAYS SO** (C18 §4.1/§4.2, stated in the ruling rather than discovered later): **no slot list here is final, including the list of wiring casualties**, and the six land by name as additions to the same table, never a second document **T84-am3 · batch 43 — the `PEND` chip recorded, and a prior question that decides its remedy.** **Member recorded:** chip `PEND`, **6 px over**, **digit-free** — so tabular does not move it and it **holds the ship, not the wiring**, exactly per T82-d's split; routing unchanged (span, then size, never the copy), magnitude to T74's table. **But: is `PEND` AUTHORED, or is it `PENDING` ALREADY TRUNCATED?** Not cosmetic. **If authored** — a state word deliberately abbreviated for a chip — it is a 6 px overrun and nothing more, and T74 takes it. **If `PENDING` clipped** — the surface is displaying **an abbreviation nobody authored**, which is G1's class and T84's (the deck exists so truncation is never reached, and a state word is the last string that should be guessed at by a measurer); a state chip gets an **authored** short form, never a clipped one, **and the box would be over by considerably more than 6 px, since 6 px is the overrun of the ALREADY-SHORTENED string.** **DISPOSITIONS PRE-COMMITTED: authored → T74 with the others, no further ruling; truncated → it returns here as a COPY item, this seat authors the short form (G1's precedent — the DD owns the statement forms), and the 6 px is re-measured against the authored string rather than the clipped one.** **S65 is the neighbouring case worth reading first** — the laptop ruled `PENDING`'s treatment at composition level and settled that PENDING is structure; the TV's chip is the same word doing the same job one surface over. **Probe exit crash (x2) — acknowledged, post-phase, holds nothing, with ONE condition on the phrase "data intact":** R43 made it standing that a determinism or baseline result is **written to a file in the same step that produces it**; if the probe's output was written that way, *intact* is verifiable and this is bookkeeping — if it was recovered from a terminal buffer after the crash, it is an assertion about data from a process that then died, and **the sweep numbers resting on it inherit the doubt. Say which** — the whole T82 finding survived its own editor crash on exactly this distinction **T84-am4 · batch 44 — `PEND` is STRUCK, and the self-catch names a class that striking one row does not dispose of.** **STRUCK:** enumerated from every call site, the chip never renders `PEND` — nor `LIVE`, `WON` or `LOST`. The 6 px row was measured against **a string that cannot render**: no overrun, no remedy, no T74 entry. **TV caught this in its own instrument and reported it against its own number**, which is the discipline this register exists to reward. **The class:** the sweep tests each box against *the longest renderable form*, and its generator produced a form that is not renderable — **two directions follow and the second is the dangerous one.** **Over-generation** (strings tested that no call site can produce) costs phantom overruns and work scheduled against nothing; `PEND` is this, caught. **Under-generation** (strings a call site CAN produce that the generator never tested) costs **a box certified as fitting that overruns in play** — and **nothing about the `PEND` catch bounds that direction**, a generator not derived from call sites being able to fail both ways at once. **Ruled — a TRACEABILITY PASS, bounded to what matters: every sweep row whose number anyone has acted on or is scheduled to act on is confirmed against a call site, in both directions** — `RiskPays` (39.8 px, a live T74 magnitude), `LegRowLine0` (1.8 px, relief already landed and wiring-gating), `MARKET SUSPENDED`, and any row the six-slot additions produced. **Not a re-run of the sweep — an inventory naming its members** (C18 §4.1), the same deliverable V6 owes and for the same reason. **Named consequence, small but it should be said: `LegRowLine0`'s relief landed on a number this pass has not yet confirmed** — if it was measured against an untraceable string the relief may have been unnecessary or mis-sized; it is committed and harmless in the unnecessary direction, and it is why the pass covers ACTED-ON rows first rather than sweeping everything. **PROBE EXIT CRASH — CLOSED:** data written before the crash, corroborated twice with Unity out of the path, **the condition met exactly as stated** and no doubt inherited by the sweep numbers — R43's durable-file-in-the-same-step practice paying out, and the second time in two days a finding survived its own crash because the data was written where a crash could not reach it **T74-am3 · batch 56 — THE FIVE SURVIVORS DISPOSITIONED, and the money control's REAL defect.** **The pattern TV named is the most valuable line in the docket and it is ruled:** *the fourth consecutive correct ruling on this surface to make a box worse* is **not four numbers, it is one mechanism** — every correct ruling that adds a required element to a control makes a box sized before that requirement worse; **the rulings are not wrong and the boxes are not unlucky, the boxes encode an older contract.** Promoted at **C46-am**. **THE MONEY CONTROL: THE MEMBERS STOP SHARING ONE RECTANGLE.** Figure and status word are anchored from **opposite edges of ONE 241.0px box**, so **each one's slack is the other's overrun and any pair of long strings collides** — at rest 45.0, mid-tween 47.8, held preview 198.5 — **and `CASHED OUT $1,240` alone is 255.6, overrunning the box by 14.6 with NO second member at all.** **Ruled: figure and status word take SEPARATE ROWS**; §6.1's *one fixed rectangle owning all six states, never reflows* is untouched, **a two-row rectangle being still fixed and still never reflowing.** **Third time the same structural answer has been right** — the intervention prompt became a list, `TakeoverSub` becomes one, now this: **N INDEPENDENT STRINGS ARE NOT ONE ROW.** Height **measured before it lands**. **`MARKET SUSPENDED`'s 26.7px is likely retired by the same change** — it owns the slot exclusively (T43), so on its own row it has the full width; measured, not assumed. **THE FIVE (T89-D — resolved or signed, no silent survivors): `TakeoverSub` 174.8 — COMPOSITION, not span: it is a LIST**, rendering the ticket's legs joined, and TV correctly reports **it has NO BOUNDED WORST CASE AT ALL** — an unbounded string in a fixed box is not a sizing question; one leg per row, and **if capped the cap prints its own count** (C19's ruled exception). **`RiskPays` 47.5 — T74, with a named prior question: the payout magnitude is UNBOUNDED** (parlay-multiplied), and span or size cannot answer an unbounded string either — **a money-abbreviation ruling is owed and it is this seat's**, routed and not decided here. **`LegRowNeed0` 40.9 — T74, span then size**; bounded, digit-free, T84(a)'s own defect, **never the copy**. **`CashOut` 26.7 — expected to retire on the two-row composition**, re-measured there. **`LegRowState0` 4.7 — T74, span or size; TRACKING IS NOT THE LEVER**: .100em on this slot is ratified label treatment under the closed clause, and **un-ruling a ratified value to buy 4.7px is the move T85 exists to prevent.** **TWO NAMED UNBOUNDED CASES — `TakeoverSub` and `RiskPays` — are the sweep's honest limit**, disclosed by TV rather than found later; **neither is closed by a magnitude and both need a BOUND or a COMPOSITION, not a number** **T84-am5 · batch 56 — `LegRowLine0`: THE PRE-COMMITTED FIRST ARM FIRES.** `BRICKLAYERS ANYTIME` **cannot be emitted by `{Surname} ANYTIME`**; the real widest form is `UNDER 10.5 CORNERS` at 144.3 in a 147.0 box. **The disposition pre-committed at T89 fires exactly as written: the relief was UNNECESSARY, not mis-sized — it STANDS, the box re-verifies, and it re-verifies as FITTING.** No revert, no fresh docket, phase untouched. **The traceability pass earned its place on this one row alone** — it removed a slot from the overrun table by finding that **the string it failed on could not exist**; overrunning slots **7 → 5**, and one of the two that left did so **because a measurement was wrong rather than because anything was fixed** **T74-am4 · batch 57 — `RiskPays`: THE WORD *UNBOUNDED* IS THE WRONG ONE, and the composition is the fourth instance of one answer.** `PotentialPayout` is parlay-multiplied so the sweep correctly reports no bounded worst case — **but parlay multiplication is not UNBOUNDED, it is UN-ENUMERATED.** `MaxLegs` is finite (4), the stake has a ceiling, and every leg's odds come from a pricing model with its own range, so **the largest renderable payout is ARITHMETIC — a product of finite terms.** **Nobody has computed it, which is a different problem from it not existing**, and it is C18 §4.1's one level up: an inventory that does not name its members. **This seat is not designing around infinity when the number is a multiplication away.** **OWED, and cheap: the maximum renderable payout, computed from `MaxLegs`, the stake ceiling and the odds range** — then the box is sized against **the longest renderable form** (C46, T89-B) and this stops being a design question at all. **COMPOSITION RULED: `RISK` and `PAYS` take SEPARATE ROWS.** `RISK $1,234  PAYS $12,340` is **two labels and two figures in one row** at 296.5 in a 249.0px box — **N independent strings are not one row**, the fourth instance today after the intervention prompt, the money control and `TakeoverSub`; each figure then has the row's full width instead of sharing it with a sibling whose slack is its overrun. **ANCHORING, taken from this surface's OWN existing pattern: label left, figure RIGHT-ANCHORED.** Not invented — it is the clock's shape measured on the Phase T pair (T75-am2: *right-anchored, ink right edge constant while the left edge travels*): **a right-anchored figure grows LEFTWARD into its own row's slack rather than overflowing rightward off the box**, so the binding constraint becomes *figure meets label* rather than *figure meets box edge*, which is far later and is a constraint the composition can state. **It also pairs correctly with tabular figures** — T82 made digit advances equal, so a right-anchored tabular figure grows in **exact digit-width steps** and the label's clearance is predictable rather than content-dependent. **`RISK` is the stable half** (bounded by the stake ceiling) **and `PAYS` the variable one**, so only one row needs the headroom. **DISPOSITIONS PRE-COMMITTED on the number nobody has computed yet: the maximum renderable payout fits its right-anchored row → the box is sized against it, recorded as the longest renderable form, and this CLOSES with no further ruling; it does not fit → the span is re-derived ONCE AT DESIGN TIME** (§5.1 makes that explicitly legal) **or the composition changes again — and ABBREVIATION STAYS REFUSED IN BOTH BRANCHES**, a span that cannot be found making this a **C16 classification** where a wider row is a design cost and not a platform impossibility: **expensive, never impossible. Neither branch reopens C49** **T74-am5 · batch 59 — THE TWO-ROW FORM IS WITHDRAWN; ONE ROW, BOTH ENDS ANCHORED. Branch 2 triggers and the answer is inside batch 57's own other half.** **First, §1.5: this is C46-am violated by its author one batch after writing it** — that clause says *when a ruling adds an element to a control, the box's fit is re-derived IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE RULING* — and this seat ruled `RiskPays` into two rows **on WIDTH and re-derived no HEIGHT**, so two 24px rows need 60.0 in a 40.0 footer, over by 20. **Batch 57 ruled TWO things — separate rows AND label-left/figure-right-anchored — and the second makes the first unnecessary, which this seat did not see.** `RISK $1,234     PAYS $12,340` measures 296.5 **as one concatenated string with authored spacing in the middle**; **anchor `RISK` to the row's left edge and `PAYS` to its right and the authored gap CEASES TO EXIST**, the slack living between them where it costs nothing — **the binding constraint stops being 296.5 and becomes `RISK`'s ink plus `PAYS`'s ink**, the same content without the spacer. **RULED: ONE ROW, `RISK` left-anchored, `PAYS` right-anchored, the gap unauthored and variable.** **Better on its own terms, not merely cheaper** — two money figures at the two ends of a footer, breathing apart, is a cleaner composition than two rows crammed into 40px, and it keeps `PAYS` right-anchored so it grows leftward **in exact digit-width steps against the tabular set** (T82). **The height problem DISSOLVES rather than being paid for:** no band grows, no size moves, no deviation signs. **PRE-COMMITTED so the measurement decides without another round trip: the two inks fit 249.0 anchored → done, one row, no height question, nothing else moves; they do NOT fit → this IS the size-authority question and it goes to T74 proper with the fact floor stated in the same breath, ABBREVIATION STAYING REFUSED (C49), and the footer does NOT grow to accommodate a spacer that no longer exists** **T84-am6 · batch 59 — THE MONEY CONTROL'S 3px: THE QUESTION IS WHERE THE 3px LANDS.** 55.0 in a 52.0 grid row, **built and rendering**, failing the sweep's standard — and **§1.5 again, the same clause and the same batch: this seat ruled the two-row form on WIDTH and re-derived no HEIGHT.** **The one fact that decides it is not in evidence here: does the 3px land in the row's OWN PADDING, or on a NEIGHBOUR?** This whole phase has turned on that distinction — **a box overrunning into its own margin is a MAGNITUDE; a box overrunning onto its neighbour is a COLLISION**, and collisions are what T84 blocks on, having been founded on two of them. **PRE-COMMITTED BOTH WAYS: (1) it lands in the control's own padding, touching nothing → SIGNED C16 DEVIATION** per T89-D's own pre-commitment that a signed deviation is acceptable for this grant — **named cost 3.0px of the money control's vertical margin, expiry the deferred sizing pass (T74), and THE PHASE PROCEEDS**, since holding a completed migration on 3px of padding is the shape C43's reasoning was written against; **(2) it lands on a NEIGHBOUR → it is a COLLISION and it is FIXED, not signed** — **leading is the first lever and it is cheap, line advance not being a ruled value on this surface** (§4.1 rules faces and sizes, not leading), so tightening 1.5px per row touches no ruled number and needs no T74, and only if leading cannot carry it does this become a size question. **On the four-element geometry option TV held: NOT ruled here, because it is not in evidence at this seat and this seat has refused to rule geometry it has not seen four times this week** — if branch 2 fires and leading cannot carry the 3px, **send it and it is ruled on sight**; branch 1 likely makes it unnecessary, and **holding it rather than building it was right either way** **T74-am6 · batch 60 — `RiskPays`: BRANCH 2 FIRES. T74 PROPER, WITH THE FACT FLOOR IN THE SAME BREATH.** Pre-committed at T74-am5 and it lands exactly as written. **Bank $10,000: RISK 138.4 + PAYS 239.7 = 378.1 against 249.0, over by 129.1. TYPICAL: 124.7 + 145.9 = 270.6, OVER BY 21.6.** **Each half fits ALONE** (138.4 and 239.7 in 249.0); **it is the pair that does not.** **The one-row both-ends-anchored form was RIGHT and it is NOT ENOUGH** — it removed the authored spacer, which was the thing being measured rather than the content, and the remaining constraint is ink plus ink exactly as T74-am5 predicted. **That is a pre-commitment written as a TEST rather than a hope, returning the answer this seat did not want.** **And the fact floor is NOT a tail case: `$1,234` staked paying `$12,340` is a plain 10x parlay, so THE FOOTER COLLIDES AT ORDINARY VALUES** — the half that makes this urgent rather than theoretical. **RULED: `RiskPays` goes to T74 PROPER as its first named magnitude, with the fact floor 378.1px against a 249.0px row ON THE RECORD.** Stated plainly so T74 begins from the truth: **the fact floor exceeds the locked column by more than half the column again, so NO SPAN INSIDE THE CURRENT WIDTH CAN CARRY IT** — T74 is choosing between the ticket column's outer width (**locked** — T46, R30 — and a change there is Allen's) and a composition that does not put both money facts on one row. **All three pre-commitments hold and none is revisited: ABBREVIATION STAYS REFUSED (C49); the copy is not reopened (§4 / T24-am); the footer does not grow for a spacer that no longer exists.** **Added to this table by name on the frames rather than by assumption: `MARKET SUSPENDED` still visibly crosses the column's right edge** in both after-sets on every seed — T74-am3 expected the two-row change to retire its 26.7px and said *measured, not assumed*; measured, it is NOT retired, and its current number is owed

body: The 12 unowned slots | **Granted — ruled regular, not defaulted; three carve-outs** · DD 2026-08-11 batch 32. Canon names 7 condensed + 4 regular roles of 23 slot types; twelve rendered regular by defaulting rather than by ruling — the finding above the item is that half the surface's type had no owner (C18's subject). **Carve-out 1 — `Clock`** and **carve-out 2 — `BigAmount`**: named by §4's tabular mandate (scores, clocks, money and counts all change in place); regular is almost certainly right for both, so the default CONFIRMS rather than conflicts — but each is verified tabular on the built face, on frames. A figure slot ruled by default and never checked for `tnum` is S29's defect exactly. **Carve-out 3 — `CashOutStatus`**: the one member inside a ruled control (§6.1, the money control, six states); its neighbour the cash-out figure is a named condensed role taking Bold 700 under T73, so the default puts two faces inside one control. Not rulable from the record — **shown on the before/after pair, disposition PRE-COMMITTED**: reads as two voices inside one control → moves to condensed; reads as label-and-figure → the default stands. `MomentumLabel` is not in question (cites canon directly, correctly excluded). Owning-doc consequence: §4.1 carries all 23 slots with their faces. *(Carve-outs transcribed into the tables 2026-08-11 batch 33 — the row previously read "as written in the batch file", which under C22 left their substance in a draft; recorded as the seat's own error §1.5, and it is why T75-am arrived in the shape it did. Swept: the only such row in the register.)* | batch 32 **T75-am · batch 33 — the `BigAmount` carve-out discharges BY CONSTRUCTION; the defect was the UNIT, not the frame (§1.5).** TV routed it rather than quietly skipping: `_tBigAmount` renders nothing (T68-am/T71 moved both payoff figures into the cash-out slot; orphaned at declaration, flagged in the orphaning commit, and the suite now asserts nothing writes a figure back to it) — no before-set frame, no possible after-set frame. **But the carve-out never needed one.** T75 wrote it "per slot"; the tabular property lives on the FONT ASSET. The surface generates exactly three assets and "regular" names ONE (`EncodeSans SDF`); a static TMP asset bakes one named instance, so there is no per-slot tabular switch to get wrong. C33's family one level over — a REQUIREMENT states the unit its property lives in (not promoted; one case). Ruled: (1) `Clock` renders and is framed — verifying tabular on the regular asset at `Clock` verifies THE ASSET; (2) `BigAmount` discharges on the shared-asset invariant — an assertion that its assigned asset is the same object as `Clock`'s, not a frame (R39's closes-by-construction pattern, off one shared base); (3) **NOT waived** — if its asset is not the shared regular asset the carve-out reverts in full and the slot may not ship on the default; both branches PRE-COMMITTED before the after-set lands; (4) `Clock`'s half unchanged and still owed on frames. **On the precedent:** S63-am2 is the right SHAPE (pre-commit before the evidence) and TV cited it correctly, but its OUTCOME does not transfer — S63's cue was a behaviour whose whole value was being seen, so unseen meant worthless and it was struck; a slot is a container whose face assignment has value the moment anything writes to it. **Cannot-be-framed decides which instrument certifies the thing, never whether it survives** **T75-am2 · batch 34 — the before-set read; what this half can and cannot say.** `Clock`: **the before half supplies BASELINE ONLY and cannot answer the carve-out**, by C15's own founding premise — `233bf7a` generated the four TMP assets and wired none (that is T-3), so these are legacy `UI.Text` frames, and tabular is UNREACHABLE pre-TMP by construction. The carve-out reads on the AFTER half alone, with this half as contrast (the docket's "`goal` and `sat-down` carry it" is true of the baseline, not the verification). Solid across 100+ frames: the clock slot is **right-anchored, ink right edge constant at x≈2343–2348** while the left edge travels, so a width change surfaces at the LEFT edge. **Confounded and returned unadjudicated (§2.6):** grouping clock strings by character count via column-gap glyph segmentation fails — **bloom merges adjacent glyphs into single runs**, so run-count is not character-count and the groups are not what they claim; the apparent width spread is NOT evidence either way and is not converted to a number. **Instrument owed, cheap:** the harness emits the clock STRING with each frame (filename or sidecar); then the test is one subtraction with no inference from pixels — *within a set of equal-character-count strings in a right-anchored slot, the left ink edge is invariant iff the digits are tabular*. Both branches PRE-COMMITTED: left edge invariant within a group → carve-out discharges; left edge moves → regular is wrong for this slot regardless of how the default was reached. `CashOutStatus`: baseline recorded on `cashout-actionable` — the control's two members render **in one face today, separated by value and size only** (`CASH OUT $131` gold vs the state word `HOLD E`/`MARKET SUSPENDED` in low-value grey). So the after-set does not introduce a distinction into an undifferentiated control; it adds a FACE split on top of a VALUE split that already exists and already works. The pre-commitment stands unchanged, but the question it answers is **"does a second face add a voice the control did not have"** — not "are these two distinguishable", which the before half already answers yes without any face difference **T75-am3 · batch 38 — the `Clock` carve-out is ANSWERED here, not on the after-set; and BOTH branches of its pre-commitment were defective (§1.5, this seat's).** T75-am2 pre-committed *left edge invariant within a group → discharges; left edge moves → regular is wrong for this slot regardless of how the default was reached*. T82's three measurements falsify both halves. **Branch 1's condition is UNREACHABLE** — no face available on this surface produces an invariant left edge, both being proportional at ~0.24 em, so the instrument could not have shown the success it was looking for (**C37's shape applied to the POSITIVE branch**: a test whose pass condition is unreachable certifies nothing by failing). **Branch 2's conclusion does NOT FOLLOW** — the left edge moves under regular AND under condensed, so the observation cannot discriminate the face assignment, which is the only thing branch 2 concludes about; executing it would have bought a different proportional face and called it a fix. Recorded as the ruling's defect, not the lane's — TV routed the question rather than quietly answering it. **Corrected disposition: the left edge moves → the mandate is unmet by the STACK, not by the slot's face assignment.** `Clock` stays **Regular** on §4's own reasoning (regular is the face the mandate wants); the tabular property is delivered at the ASSET per T82 and never by a face swap. The after-set frames become **corroboration, not the deciding instrument**. **The owed harness clock-string emission is NOT retired — it is RE-POINTED**: batch 34 owed it so the carve-out could be tested by subtraction instead of the glyph segmentation bloom confounded; it now becomes **the acceptance test for T82's fix** — within a set of equal-character-count strings in a right-anchored slot, the left ink edge is invariant iff the digits are tabular. Same instrument, same subtraction, verifying the remedy instead of deciding the carve-out. **`BigAmount`:** T75-am's shared-asset invariant does the work a second time — the fix lands on the asset, so any slot on that asset inherits it with no per-slot work; moot in practice until T79 resolves, since the element renders nothing today **T75-am4 · batch 39 — the `CashOutStatus` pre-commitment is RETURNED UNADJUDICATED (§2.6); NEITHER BRANCH FIRES.** T75-am2 pre-committed *reads as two voices inside one control → moves to condensed; reads as label-and-figure → the default stands*. On the after frames the two members **OVERLAP** — `CASH OUT $131OLD E` (T84) — and a question about whether a second face adds a voice **cannot be read through a collision: the confound sits in the same channel as the answer.** This is a **VOID, not a null** (C37's distinction) — the instrument could not have resolved either outcome in this state, so its silence is not evidence for the default and the default does not stand by walkover. **The pre-commitment survives unchanged and re-reads on the frames that follow T84's fix** — no new ruling required, which is the entire point of having pre-committed it before the evidence **T75-am5 · batch 58 — THE ASSET COUNT WAS THREE AND IT IS FOUR; body: The mandatory tabular figures are unreachable on the shipped stack | **RULED — the mandate STANDS unamended; the atlas ships the font's own tabular glyphs; the "cannot" is EXPENSIVE, not impossible** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 38, on TV's three-way measurement at `cb84278`. **Measurement ACCEPTED in full, and it corroborates harder than the docket claimed.** Three instruments, two sharing no machinery: an in-engine digit probe, `hmtx` advances read through `cmap` with no editor, and a GSUB enumeration — which is why the finding survives its own editor crash, named here as the discipline to copy. The docket left the file-versus-engine gap as a hand-wave (*"≈87 px against the 93 px measured, the difference being the instance"*); **checked at this seat it is exact.** Predicting each measured spread from `hmtx` and taking the ratio gives **1.0704 at Regular 36pt AND 1.0704 at Regular 28pt; 0.998 at Condensed 29pt AND 0.998 at Condensed 19pt** — **constant across sizes within each face, to four figures**, which is the signature of a uniform instance scale and therefore exactly the cause the docket named. The two instruments do not roughly agree, they agree exactly up to one scale factor per face, and **that scale factor IS the instance** (Condensed renders its file default; Regular renders an instance ~7% wider in advance). Proportionality is over-determined, not merely corroborated. **C44-clean** — reported as independent corroboration with the residual named, never as a bound judging a reading. **Classification (C16), because the headline and the body disagree:** the title says tabular *cannot be reached*; the body says *"unreachable by any in-scope choice"* and, decisively, *"closing it requires a decision about how the glyphs are obtained rather than a line of code"* — **that sentence IS C16's classification, stated by the lane, and it is adopted as this ruling's reasoning.** `tnum` at runtime is genuinely **impossible** (TMP's `OTL_FeatureTag` declares only `kern`, `liga`, `mark`, `mkmk`; no tag or property exposes one) — but tabular figures on this surface are **possible**, because the glyphs are drawn, present in GSUB and addressable at build time. Therefore **expensive, not impossible: no signed deviation is issued and none is needed.** The headline overshoots the body; recorded as a classification correction and nothing more — the lane surfaced the refuting route itself and recommended it, the opposite of a finding that hides its own escape. **The mandate is NOT amended:** the twitch is 46–93 px across ten digits at rendered sizes, not marginal; **T11 selected the face on this exact criterion** with Saira disqualified for lacking `tnum`, so amending now would retroactively decide the criterion the face was chosen on does not matter; and a faithful route exists — C16 does not let convenience reclassify itself as impossibility. **Option (b) `<mspace>` REFUSED** — forcing one advance imposes a metric **the family does not contain**, which is §4's *no synthesised styling* in the spacing channel (a synthesised bold is a smear, an italic a shear, a monospace the third of the same thing), and it hits letters in mixed strings: `CASH OUT $183` is the money control that cost four batches at T63/T68/T68-am/T71, and monospacing its label to fix its figures is **C10's shape exactly**. **Option (c) amend-the-mandate REFUSED, held as the named fallback with its condition PRE-COMMITTED before the build attempt:** if (a) proves unbuildable — the substitution cannot be resolved at generation time, or the tabular glyphs are not addressable in the generated set despite their GSUB presence — the classification changes to genuinely impossible and (c) returns as a **C16 signed deviation with a named cost and an expiry**; not before, and never on difficulty. **Option (a) GRANTED as the route** — the atlas ships the font's own tabular digits as its default set, the substitution resolved at build time with U+0030–0039 mapped to the tabular glyph indices. These are the figures **the type designer drew**, which is what separates it from (b). **The ruling is the OUTCOME, not the mechanism:** either the Unity generator resolving the substitution or a pre-processed static instance with the feature frozen and committed as the atlas source — **the lane picks**; this seat does not choose a build method. **Four conditions.** (1) **The unit is the ASSET, not the slot** — T75-am established it and this confirms it one level down; **every generated asset any figure slot renders on takes the tabular set, and the inventory NAMES ITS MEMBERS** (C18 §4.1), not "the atlas": the condensed Bold 700 asset carries `CashOut`, the surface's money figure, and an inventory naming two assets while missing a third ships a control that still twitches. (2) **Digits alone satisfy the mandate** — digits are the characters that change, `$`, `:` and separators are constant and need nothing; the mandate's content is **equal advance among digits**, not constant string width, so a score going 9 to 10 adds a character and widens and that is layout (T75-am2's right-anchor), never a tabular failure. (3) **One variable** — `lnum` is also present; figure STYLE does not move in this commit, tabular only. (4) **§3.5 binds the same commit** — a width change obliges the layout depending on it to be re-derived in the same commit, and a zone that cannot hold the widened figure routes to T74, never a tune inside the tabular commit. **Licensing: no new question** (same OFL 1.1 files already subsetted into SDF atlases; a build-time feature application is the same class of operation on the same files) — informational, since T11 recorded a licence basis. **Free by-product, ROUTED not ruled:** the constant per-face ratio is a **width-axis fingerprint of the rendered instance obtained without frames**, which is the desk measurement T78-am owes — bounded twice so nobody over-reads it: **advance alone cannot separate weight from width** (a heavier instance at one width is wider too, which is why T78-am asked for stem width AND width axis; this supplies one channel), and **which asset `cb84278` loaded decides what the number means** (at T-5 the canon faces may already be wired, in which case the ratio describes the migrated instance, not the legacy base T78 asked about). Lands in the deferred sizing pass with the rest of T78-am. **Sequencing: the build lands AFTER the after-set is shot** — not in Phase T, whose variable is a closed list of three under T81 with C43-am(3) forbidding anything joining afterwards; frozen in the interim per **T80-am2**. **FALSIFICATION PRE-COMMITTED, before the evidence was read (§1.5's discipline, and the reason it is stated here rather than after):** the after-set landed at `dd-import/tv-phase-t-after-2026-08-12/` while this ruling was being transcribed, and it **carries `clock-strings.tsv`** — the harness instrument owed since batch 34, now built. This ruling makes a checkable prediction about that file. At the moment of writing, **this seat has counted the set's files and opened none of them.** Pre-committed both ways: **within a group of equal-character-count clock strings in the right-anchored slot, the left ink edge MOVES** — that is what proportional digits mean and it is what T82 asserts; observing it **corroborates** T82 and T75-am3 and closes the `Clock` carve-out on rendered evidence as well as on the files. **If the left ink edge is instead INVARIANT within an equal-character-count group, T82's premise is wrong on the rendered surface** and this whole ruling re-opens — the atlas grant, the mandate's delivery clause and T75-am3's corrected disposition together — because the shipped stack would then be reaching a tabular advance by some path none of the three measurements found. Not a caveat: a stated way to be wrong, on evidence already on disk **T82-a · batch 39 — THE FALSIFIER FIRED AND T82 SURVIVED IT.** Measured at this seat on the after-set's `clock-strings.tsv` plus its frames: 3-char `DD'` group **left-edge spread 22.0 px** where tabular predicts ~0; **correlation between ink width and the `hmtx` predicted advance +0.9824**; **residual sd about the fit 1.04 px**; narrowest `71'` 58.0 px to widest `90'` 80.0 px, **measured delta 22.0 px against 21.2 px predicted from the font's own advance table**; clock right edge spread 5 px, so the right-anchor holds. The left edge moves, and it moves by the amount the advance table predicts, to about a pixel. **A third instrument, sharing nothing with the two that produced the finding, in a third place.** Coverage stated (C28): 54 of 156 non-empty-clock frames measured, 37 in the clean subset, the remainder dropped where bloom merged the separator isolating the clock; the instrument's resolution is the 1.04 px residual, not the raw detection spread. **T75-am3's corrected disposition is confirmed on rendered evidence** — the left edge moves under the canon face, so the mandate is unmet by the STACK exactly as ruled, not by `Clock`'s face assignment **T82-b · batch 40 — the DERIVED FONT LANDED; source verified, and one line closes it.** `tnum` resolved at build time, **every digit exactly 1000 units, spread 0, cmap-only change** — the atlas route built exactly as granted: the font's own tabular glyphs, no outline invented, and a cmap-only diff is the narrowest possible expression of it. The unit is right, the change landing on the **asset** where T75-am put the property. **§2.5 holds the close open by one line** — *a source string is not a rendered element*; "every digit 1000 units, spread 0" measures the FILE, which is **necessary and not sufficient**, and is the same clause that made T82 a ruling rather than a note. **What closes it, with the instrument already built:** T75-am3's rendered line — within a set of equal-character-count clock strings in the right-anchored slot, **the left ink edge is INVARIANT**; the after-set already proved that instrument works by measuring the proportional case at 22.0 px spread on a 1.04 px residual, and the tabular case is the same measurement expecting ~0. **If TV's report carries that line, T82 CLOSES on this evidence; if not, one line is owed and nothing else.** **Still owed regardless, unchanged from the grant: the ASSET INVENTORY naming its members** — every generated asset any figure slot renders on, confirmed tabular, **including the condensed Bold 700 asset carrying `CashOut`**; a cmap-only change is per-file, three assets need three confirmations, and an inventory naming two of three is the defect C18 §4.1 exists for **T82-c · batch 41 — T82 does NOT close, and batch 40's close condition was this seat's to get wrong (§1.5).** TV's answer is correct and is the answer §2.5 was asking for: the derived font is proven tabular **at the font layer**, the shipped assets are **NOT wired to it** (held per the ruled sequencing). So **"mechanism accepted" matches the evidence and "the surface renders tabular" does not** — nothing on screen has changed, and **the rendered left-ink-edge line cannot run meaningfully until wiring** because there is nothing for it to measure. **Batch 40 wrote the close condition as though the assets were wired; the principle underneath it is RULED GENERAL.** TV reports `(99%)` is **the same quantity class as T16's subject at a different site** — a leg's probability at a decision prompt rather than on the momentum tape — and asks whether T16 reaches beyond the tape. **It does, but *does ruling X reach site Y* is exactly the question S67 was written about** (*a ruling can only reach the call sites that route through the thing it was ruled on*); T16 was ruled on the tape, extending it by analogy is the move S67 warns against, and **the honest way to cover the second site is to rule the principle directly and name T16 as its first instance.** **THE PRINCIPLE: the match theatre prints FACTS and OFFERS. It does not print OPINIONS.** A **price is an offer** — a thing the house stands behind, which the player can transact against; **a probability is the house's opinion** about an outcome with nothing attached to it. The player can take or leave a price; he can only agree or disagree with an opinion, and **this surface does not ask him to do that.** **This explains T16, T23 and T32(4) in one line** — win-probability numeral out, backed-player numeral out, the 10px numeral deleted — where before there were three separate deletions that happened to rhyme; `SEND TO REVIEW (99%)` is an instruction wearing a number.** Everything else he needs is already on screen and is his to read: score, clock, legs, prices, state. **ROUTED NOT RULED, two things visible from here: (1) a 99% option contains no decision** — whatever it costs, an option that succeeds ~always is pressed ~always, a balance question for the lane that owns the mechanic, named only because it was visible in the string; title: The intervention prompt commits an irreversible spend on one frame of input, and its copy promises otherwise
state_raw: **RULED — VIOLATION; the queued T22 question, which the find turns from a boundary case into a defect** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 50. **The copy says `HOLD`. The input is `wasPressedThisFrame`. A single p
body: The intervention prompt commits an irreversible spend on one frame of input, and its copy promises otherwise | **RULED — VIOLATION; the queued T22 question, which the find turns from a boundary case into a defect** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 50. **The copy says `HOLD`. The input is `wasPressedThisFrame`. A single press commits an irreversible spend the instant it fires.** **FOUR VIOLATIONS STACKED, and they are not one violation four times: (1) the copy names a SAFETY PROPERTY the input does not provide** — `HOLD` promises a preview and an abandon path and the input has neither; **worse than a wrong label**, because a wrong label misnames a thing while this misdescribes what happens when you touch it, **and the player relies on that description exactly when he is careless**. **(2) T22(c) violated — release is never confirm**, except here there is no release at all: the press IS the commit, so **there is no interval in which the player is holding something he can still abandon** — T22's safety structure is ABSENT, not weakened. **(3) T22(d) — commit is an act on the laptop**, and this commits money from the theatre. **(4) There is NO ABANDON PATH:** the first frame of input is terminal, **on a surface the player is WATCHING rather than operating**, and a control that can only be fired and never backed out of, on a seated-posture surface, **will be fired by accident.** **T59 ALREADY RULED THE PRINCIPLE ONE AXIS OVER** (*display state and input state are the same state, read from one value; accepting a declared-refused input on a money control is the worst outcome — the player gets a price the display is not showing*): T59 governed AVAILABILITY, this is the same law on the **GESTURE** axis, and **a player acting on the displayed contract gets an outcome the display did not describe** — T59's own sentence with *gesture* for *price*. Promoted to **C48**. **RULED: (a) the theatre MAY carry this commit** — T22's *commit is an act on the laptop* is not overridden, because **T22 already contemplated a theatre-side confirm and specified its shape** (*a second key during the hold; no timer, no auto-commit*), and the mechanic earns it: **a frozen shot that requires walking to the laptop is not a frozen shot.** **(b) EVERY SPENDING OPTION TAKES T22's FALLBACK GESTURE, UNCHANGED** — hold to preview, the preview showing what the option does **and what it costs** (T86-am: the basis for a decision is an offer, not an opinion); **release abandons, always**; a second key during the hold commits; **no timer, no auto-commit; a press does not commit on any of them.** **(c) The DECLINING option is not a spend and does not take the gesture** — `LET IT DIE` costs nothing and **is already what happens if the player does nothing**, so a single press is proportionate; ruled as the general shape, **the weight of the gesture matches the weight of the act**, which also stops the three reading as peers when two spend and one does not. **(d) Until the gesture is built the copy must NOT say `HOLD`** — a label describing a safety the input lacks is the defect, **but shipping the honest label on a press-to-commit control is worse than either, so the fix is the GESTURE and not the word**; if the gesture cannot land in this pass **the control does not ship**, a money control firing on one frame not being a state this surface may be seen in. **THE 380px — the answer is neither copy nor size: 635px carrying a string needing ~1015px is not a sizing miss but a composition that does not fit its zone**, which is **C46's named class** (a fixed box's unstated fits-assumption, failing). **Ruled from existing law rather than invention: THREE OPTIONS ARE A LIST, NOT A LINE** — S24 ruled exactly this shape for the scorer market (*renders as a single-column offer list, never a paired row with a dead cell*) and the reason transfers, **N offers being a list while one line is a row pretending to be a sentence**. It **solves the gesture problem in the same move**: one option per row gives each its own cost, its own key, and somewhere for a hold affordance to live. **NOT routed to T74, and the distinction matters** — T74 settles which SIZE AUTHORITY governs and nothing here asks whether the type is too big; **line-to-list is COMPOSITION, which is this seat's**, and §3.5 makes re-deriving a layout at design time explicitly legal. **Condition, stated because this seat does not have the zone: a list needs vertical room, and if the prompt's zone cannot carry three rows that returns here WITH THE ZONE'S DIMENSIONS** as a composition question, never a copy trim — §6's fixed grid still binds and the zone does not resize to content. **THE WORDING IS NOT RATIFIED: this seat does not ratify strings it has not read.** S68 is the standing lesson and it has been applied twice in two days (T85-am3 held two slots proposed on a class description rather than their text, and one of this seat's own stated reasons proved wrong while the disposition still fired) — **a voice ratification is made against the string, never against a description of it.** Send the strings and they rule on sight; **send the 380px breakdown with them** (options line alone, or the whole prompt including `SHOT FROZEN`), because the list ruling changes the arithmetic and the two are answered differently. **Nothing blocks** — the gesture ruling and the list direction are both actionable now and neither waits on the wording **T88-am · batch 56 — THE ZONE, THE KEY, THE STRINGS — and a defect in the fix that is C48's OWN defect.** **`HOLD N LET IT DIE` IS WRONG BY THE RULING THIS ARC PRODUCED:** T88(c) ruled the declining option **does not take the gesture** (it costs nothing and is already what happens if he does nothing, so a single press is proportionate), the string was carried forward under *unchanged* and **never met T88(c)** — **so the prompt prints `HOLD` over an input that is a PRESS, which is precisely the copy-promises-a-gesture-the-input-does-not-implement defect C48 was written for, surviving inside the pass that fixed it.** **RULED: `N LET IT DIE`**, no `HOLD`; the two spending rows keep theirs and **the difference between the rows now does real work — it tells him which options cost him something.** *Recorded without blame — it was listed as unchanged and unchanged was true; **a string that never meets the ruling that changed its class is the same defect one level up**, and the *listed so the set is the whole set* section is where it was caught.* **THE 20px: `SHOT FROZEN` LEAVES THE ZONE; THE ZONE DOES NOT GROW.** Four reasons stacking: **the stage already says it** (the shot is frozen on screen, this surface shows state and lets him read it — T33's shape — and a title announcing what the frame displays is the restatement class S37/S58/T69/T70 each ruled); **growing the zone spends a locked dimension to restate it** (R30, and §6's grid does not resize to content); **it removes the worst case rather than affording it** — three option rows measure 82.5 in a 90.0 zone and fit **in EVERY ownership combination**, where C46 forbids leaning on the common case; and the held preview keeps 35.0 spare. **If a word is still wanted the EVENT STRIP is its home** (§8's *one authored line explaining the latest move*, which is what a frozen shot is) — **measured before it lands, not asserted** (T89's bar), and not required, since the frame may carry the moment alone. **THE CONFIRM KEY: `ENTER` — RATIFIED**, both halves of TV's reasoning adopted: **bound to nothing** in the room lane's shared action asset so the gesture reserves no key the room uses, and **one commit key across both money controls** keeps the two contracts readable as the same contract — **standing: the studio has ONE commit key, not one per control**; a re-bind is one line plus two strings, which is the right shape for a decision that may later meet a platform this seat has no evidence about. **STRINGS RATIFIED:** `HOLD M MULLIGAN (ONE MULLIGAN SLIP)` (T88(b)'s cost, in `RelicCatalog`'s own name and the whistle's ruled parenthetical form, **no abbreviation coined** — G1's defect class avoided rather than survived); `ENTER CONFIRMS · RELEASE ABANDONS` (**states BOTH halves of the contract**, which is what C48 asks of a label; declarative, not second person; the register's own separator); `ENTER TO CASH OUT` (**ratified as copy** — and it breaks its box, see T74-am3). **`ENTER TO CASH OUT`'s reasoning is ENDORSED and is the lane applying C48 to a case this seat did not rule:** *under a held preview, `HOLD E` tells the player to do the thing he is already doing and never says how to finish it.* **A contract that describes the previous moment is not a contract.** **THE LANE'S OWN DERIVED RULE RATIFIED AND NAMED — *the gesture acts on what is shown*:** it is **T59's law on the gesture's TIME axis** (display state and input state are one state), since **a hold that outlives the thing it was started against is a press on a screen that has moved.** Standing precondition on every held gesture | batch 50

body: The stats panel's own composition — raised, not ruled | **RAISED; the condition for ruling it named** · DD 2026-08-15 batch 85. **This seat has now seen the panel, so it can say something; it has seen ONE state, so it will not rule it.** **The observation: the panel is largely empty** — three rows (`GOALS`, `CORNERS`, `CARDS`) in a surface occupying most of the screen, with a large unoccupied region beneath `CARDS`. **And the state is why, at least in part: this is a moneyline leg, so corners and cards carry the unrevealed mark (`—`) — ruled behaviour off a count leg and not a defect, which TV named — but it means two of three rows show their EMPTY form, and a panel judged on that state would be judged on its thinnest possible content.** **OWED BEFORE IT IS RULED: one frame with a POPULATED count row (a corners or cards leg), so the table carries real values in every row.** **Same discipline as the 0–0 condition on this very capture: a surface shot in its emptiest state cannot be read for how it fills** | batch 85 **· RULED — THE DEAD SPACE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT STATEFUL · batch 87** (`dd-import/tv-statspanel-countrow-2026-08-15/`). **The reserved condition is met and it answers the question AGAINST the panel: `GOALS 0 | 0` · `CORNERS 2 | 1` · `CARDS — | —` — a real count row carrying real values, and the panel is as empty as it was.** The table occupies the top quarter and roughly two-thirds is unoccupied — **and it would be unoccupied with every row populated, because the table is three rows in EVERY state and the panel is sized to the screen.** **RULED: the emptiness is not the state, it is the design.** **REMEDY, and it is this surface's own legal move: the panel is sized ONCE AT DESIGN TIME to the content it carries** — §2 legalises exactly this and nothing else (*re-deriving a fixed grid constant once at design time is legal; a zone resizing in response to content is not*), **the same move that set `MatchupCardPitch` and `RelationStatementHeight`.** **THE ARGUMENT IN ONE LINE: a surface that takes the entire stage and returns three rows has not earned the stage.** **This is NOT a complaint about empty space — this studio has twice ruled emptiness correct (S52's desktop at 99.7% at-ground; the draws block's honest empty line). The objection is the EXCHANGE: he gives up the ticket column, the pitch and the scorebug, and receives a table that would fit in a quarter of what it took.** **NOT RULED: what the panel becomes** — position, edges and final height are TV's to propose; this seat has seen it in two states and will not redraw a surface it does not own. **ONE COUPLING NAMED because TV may not see it from inside the panel: if a resized panel no longer covered the scorebug, T99's conditional licence would not be needed at all — the size question and the freeze question are LINKED, named so it is weighed rather than ordered as a direction.** **RECORDED, not ruled: (a) the fullest state STILL was not shot** — `CARDS` is unrevealed off a corners leg since a one-leg ticket reveals at most goals plus one count market, and all three rows populated needs a multi-leg ticket carrying both; **not ordered, because it cannot change a finding about the panel's height against a fixed three-row table**; **(b) the `GOALS` row restores a fact the panel itself covers** — T99 ruled the row legitimate and ruled it may not justify the covering, and both stand, **but plainly: of six cells here two restate the scorebug the panel is hiding and one row is unrevealed, so the panel's novel content on a single-leg ticket is TWO NUMBERS. A scope observation for Allen, not a defect and not this seat's to rule** **· `T100-am` batch 88 — ALLEN TOOK (B): the panel's top drops below `y = 62`, the scorebug clear throughout.** **The size-and-freeze coupling batch 87 named lands exactly as named — T99's licence goes moot, the freeze survives on its own clause, and the player keeps the score.** **THE PHRASE FOLDED:** §6.6's *"opens from the HEAD OF the ticket column"* now reads as the column's SIDE, and is folded to **"opens from the ticket column"** with the reason written beside it — **a phrase that names a SEAM goes stale every time the seam moves; a phrase that names a RELATIONSHIP does not.** Same class as the DRAW cell's midpoint: a relationship built rather than a value written down. **AND THE EXTENT CLAUSE WAS NEVER AMENDED — IT WAS RESTORED, which changes the account.** §6.6 has always read *"it expands over the column and stage"* — **two regions, and the scorebug is a THIRD** (§4.1: *compact scorebug + stage* fill the right; §5.1: the stage clips to its own region). **§6.6 never licensed covering the scorebug; the shipped panel did it anyway, and Allen's placement returns it inside the line the owning doc had already drawn.** **This seat's part stated plainly: TV raised the overlap as a question and T99 answered it WITHOUT NOTICING §6.6 ALREADY SPOKE — a ruling that grants what the owning document already refused, which is precisely the defect cycle 220 named (*a ruling that never meets the owning document never meets its own surface's existing law*), from the seat that keeps citing it.** **What kept the cost at zero: T99 was ruled CONDITIONALLY, and that condition is what failed the first shoot and caught the unfrozen clock — a flat approval would have granted the overreach permanently and caught nothing.** **AND ONE MORE THING THE DOC ALREADY REQUIRED: §6.6's standing *ships at authored height with no reserved space* (T21) — so batch 87's *sized once at design time to the content it carries* is NOT a new requirement, it is T21, already in that paragraph and already binding; the panel shipped at screen height against a clause that said authored height. Recorded so the resize is understood as a RETURN to canon rather than a change of it** **· DESIGN-VERIFIED · batch 89** (`dd-import/tv-statspanel-resized-2026-08-15/`). **`(0, 0, 980, 480)` → `(0, 62, 564, 246)` — 29.5% of the area, a 70.5% reduction.** **Granted: boxes are widest measured ink plus a margin taken from a COMMITTED SWEEP rather than chosen, `pad` (32) is the only spacing value, and the vertical rhythm was untouched — batch 87's ruling executed as ruled.** **The scorebug is clear and THE PIN IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: zero overlap on BOTH axes, asserted as full 2D against live rects and deliberately not single-axis, so a later change narrowing only the vertical gap while the columns still cross is caught as the partial coverage it would be — the pin is built to *a half-covered scorebug is worse than a fully covered one*.** **And the guard that now guards nothing was KEPT: the standing condition at `SeatedDeltaTime` protects a coverage that no longer happens, retained because it is written where a future re-enlargement would be made, which is exactly when it stops being vacuous — deleting a guard because it currently guards nothing is how the T95 class recurs, and the lane said so itself**

body: `contentMargin = 16` — the panel's one invented number | **NOT RATIFIED as a constant; the proportion governs and the law already exists** · DD 2026-08-15 batch 89. **The lane named it correctly: one invented number, load-bearing, unratified. It is not ratified, and the reason is that a CONSTANT IS THE WRONG FORM for what it does.** **What 16px buys: label `MATCH STATS` 155.8 in 172 = 9.4% headroom; value `Spreadsheets` 115.3 in 132 = 12.6%.** **C46's risk is PROPORTIONAL — a face 10% wider makes every string 10% wider — so a fixed pixel margin gives its least protection exactly where the risk is greatest, on the widest string. Concretely: at 16px `MATCH STATS` survives a face ~10% wider and overflows at 11%.** **RULED: S77-am's budget governs — *stays under 80%*, whose stated reason is C46's *~20% is what absorbs a face that measures wider*. C46 is a register-level CROSS-SURFACE law, and inventing a second headroom budget for the same hazard on a different surface is one-name-per-thing broken at the level of RULES.** **So ink ≤ 80% of box: `labelW ≥ 195` (from 172), `valueW ≥ 145` (from 132), panel ~564 → ~613 — still 37% of the original 980, so the resize's win is essentially intact.** **`contentMargin` as a NAMED CONSTANT stays — the derivation reads from it rather than restating literals, which is the right shape; what changes is that it is DERIVED FROM THE RATIO, not chosen.** **AND S84 BINDS THE VALUE COLUMN, the half most likely to be missed: `MATCH STATS` is authored copy but `Zambonis`/`Spreadsheets` are TEAM NAMES — generated — and S84 rules that a cell holding a generated string is sized against the reachable maximum of its GENERATOR, never a sample taken off the surface.** **`Spreadsheets` at 115.3 is the widest string the sweep MEASURED; whether it is the widest team name that EXISTS is a different question and the pool is a fixed list. OWED: confirm it against the enumerated pool, and if a wider name exists `valueW` derives from that one** | batch 89 **· DESIGN-VERIFIED · batch 92.** **label/value 172/132 → 195/145, panel 564 → 613, area 29.5% → 32.1% — still under a third of the stage.** **`MaxInkFraction = 0.8` is ONE named constant and both widths derive from it, so a further ruling moves one number; `contentMargin` was REMOVED rather than left dead, which is the half most builds skip.** **S84's pool binding NOW GATES: 20 clubs enumerated, every one re-measured through the panel's own rendered slot — and deliberately NOT `[Explicit]`, because the C46 sweep is filter-only and never runs in routine suites, WHICH IS PRECISELY HOW A 21ST CLUB COULD HAVE OVERFLOWED UNNOTICED. body: The GOALS row — removed, and the argument is STRUCTURAL | **RULED — REMOVED** · DD 2026-08-16 batch 93. **T103 found the row duplicates a scorebug that is never covered — true, and not the strongest reason.** **THE PANEL EXISTS TO GIVE THE PER-TEAM SPLIT, AND FOR GOALS THERE IS NO SPLIT TO GIVE: `Yams 0 | Zambonis 0` and the scorebug's `YAMS 0 — 0 ZAMBONIS` are the same two numbers, in the same order, one slot apart. There is nothing to ADD, not merely something repeated** — and that holds however the panel is keyed, **which is why (c) does not dissolve it on its own and it had to be ruled.** **Every goals market is served by the scorebug directly: moneyline reads the result, BTTS reads both numbers, correct score IS the scoreline, over/under totals is their sum of two single digits. Removing the row costs no fact.** **A scorer leg takes no row either, by the same rule rather than a special case — it rides on goals, which have no split, and player stats are barred outright (§6.6, a generator-truth leak).** **THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS WHAT (c) MEANS: a ticket riding only on goals gives the panel nothing, so moneyline-only tickets — very likely the commonest — have no rows at all. RULED: the panel does not open empty; where the ticket gives it nothing its AFFORDANCE IS UNAVAILABLE and says so BEFORE the key is pressed** — **S85's law, surface-independent and made on the laptop three batches ago, and here it is knowable at all times from the ticket so it never needs discovering.** **(c) THEREFORE MAKES THE PANEL A COUNT-TICKET FEATURE — available where it has something to say, unavailable where it does not — which is also the honest answer to batch 87's scope question: it stopped being a surface that takes the stage to show two numbers, because it now only exists when it has numbers worth taking it for.** **AND THE UNREVEALED MARK SURVIVES AND CHANGES MEANING, which is the prize: `_countLedger` carries one kind and resets per leg, so a ticket may ride on more quantities than the ledger can populate and the unpopulated row keeps its `—` — but where today `—` means *this quantity is not in your ticket*, under (c) it means *your ticket rides on this and it is not revealed yet*. The mark stops meaning IRRELEVANT and starts meaning NOT YET.** **OWED, non-blocking: whether the ledger can carry more than one kind at once — an engine question that changes only how often a second row shows `—` instead of a number** | batch 93 **· `T104-am2` batch 94 — THE BLANK-ROW CONSEQUENCE, and TWO CLAUSES OF BATCH 93 ARE NOT IN THE BUILD.** **On the frame `GOALS 0 | 0` is still present, and TV's own table gives moneyline → 1 of 3 — that one row IS `GOALS`.** **Batch 93 ruled (1) `GOALS` removed — *not conditionally, not keyed — removed* — and (2) the affordance UNAVAILABLE where the ticket gives no rows. Neither is built.** **Said without complaint (the lane's report is scrupulous and is what surfaced this) but the magnitude must be corrected before it is weighed: WITH BOTH CLAUSES IN, corners+cards = 2 of 2 full · one count leg = 1 of 2 · MONEYLINE = 0 ROWS AND NO PANEL AT ALL.** **The "one row in a three-row panel" case DOES NOT EXIST under the ruling — it exists under a build that kept a row the ruling removed, so batch 87's *earned the stage* finding does not reopen.** **THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND IS A BUILD DEFECT RATHER THAN A DESIGN COST: a single-count ticket gives one blank slot, and the build produces it by CONFLATING TWO STATES batch 93 made different — a row NOT IN THE SET should have NO SLOT AT ALL (it was never bought), while a row IN THE SET BUT UNREVEALED keeps its slot and carries the mark. The build renders absent rows as blank slots (`SetStatsRow(i, "", "", "")`), so an unbought row occupies space and says nothing — precisely the distinction that made the mark worth keeping.** **RULED: THE PANEL'S HEIGHT FOLLOWS ITS ROW SET, derived once at ticket adoption from the same computation that already derives the set (`ComputeStatsRowSet()`), so it costs no new mechanism. §2 is satisfied by the argument batch 93 already made — if the SET may be per-ticket, so may a height that is a pure function of it.** **NONE of TV's three remedies is taken as offered: (iii) leaves a defect, not a cost; (ii) collapsing blanks is RIGHT for absent rows and WRONG for unrevealed ones and the build has it backwards — an unrevealed row must keep its slot or the table grows when a count is first revealed, which is the shift under the player TV correctly fears; (i) is correct and CHEAPER than priced, because the derivation exists already** **· `T104-am3` batch 96 — ALLEN RULED: `GOALS` STAYS, two rows is right.** **Batch 93's removal is OVERRULED and this seat does not re-argue it. TV caught the contradiction with the keying rule and ASKED rather than building through it, which is the behaviour that got the question in front of him at all.** **THE FORMULATION THAT MAKES THE TWO RULES AGREE, which is what the contradiction was about: `GOALS` IS A STANDING ROW, NOT A KEYED ONE — the panel is `GOALS` plus the count rows the ticket keys, and keying governs what sits BENEATH the standing row; it never governed the standing row.** So: moneyline → **1** (`GOALS`) · one count leg → **2** · corners+cards → **3**. **That is the three-row maximum the panel was already built for, and the keying rule is unchanged in its own scope — the contradiction was that batch 93 applied keying to a row that was never a keyed row.** **WHAT THIS WITHDRAWS, and it matters because both were already routed: (1) THE ZERO-ROW AFFORDANCE IS MOOT AND WITHDRAWN — with `GOALS` standing the panel is never empty, and an outstanding obligation that can no longer fire is a thing someone eventually builds; (2) "A COUNT-TICKET FEATURE" IS WITHDRAWN — the panel is available always, and the scope framing goes with it.** **WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the keying rule itself; absent keyed rows get NO SLOT while unrevealed keyed rows keep theirs and carry the mark; the height follows the rows; and `COUNTS` as the title — its justification unchanged in substance, since batch 94 grounded it on the header naming what the row labels ARE, and with `GOALS` back the rows are goals, corners and cards, all three counts. THE TITLE READS TRUER WITH THE ROW IN THAN IT DID WITH THE ROW OUT.** **Also: T103's duplication, accepted at batch 90, is now PERMANENT rather than provisional — (c) was the path that would have ended it — recorded so it is not reopened as an unfinished item.** **ONE CONSEQUENCE THE RULING DOES NOT REACH, stated once and not argued: a moneyline ticket now yields a ONE-ROW panel carrying `GOALS` alone, the row the scorebug already states two slots up in the same order. The ruling was made on the CORNERS case, where the standing row sits above a count the scorebug cannot give; the moneyline case follows from it without having been the thing decided. Noted for the record, no recommendation, nothing owed.** **CLOSING CRITERION RESTATED, superseding batch 95's *one row tall*: a corners-only ticket makes the panel EXACTLY TWO ROWS — `GOALS` and `CORNERS` — with NO blank slot beneath them, and the height is two rows tall** **· MET — DESIGN-VERIFIED, PHASE CLOSED · batch 97.** **Measured at this seat against `tv-statspanel-single-count-2026-08-15`, same seed and beat: the panel's bottom edge moves y 792 → 691, a 101px reduction — EXACTLY ONE 46px ROW PITCH at this frame's scale. The panel shrank by one ROW, not by a number someone chose. And a pitch feature now reads at y 696–741 where the panel covered it: the stage is given back measurably, not just arithmetically.** **The absent signal is distinct from the mark AT THE SOURCE — `DebugStatsRow(2)` returns `null` where a bought-but-unrevealed row returns the mark — so the blank-versus-mark distinction the lane built is KEPT and now sits UNDERNEATH a slot distinction instead of substituting for it, which is what batch 95 asked for and why both halves were worth having.** **THE MECHANISM, and the way it is built is the half that lasts: ONE FORMULA, ONE APPLICATION SITE — `StatsPanelHeight(rowCount)` derives from the last row's own y, `ResizeStatsPanel()` is the single place it is applied, and it is called from `ComputeStatsRowSet()` AT TICKET ADOPTION, where the row set becomes known. 246 stops being a fixed value and becomes a MAXIMUM — the batch-87-to-93 tension resolved rather than worked around.** **AND THE LANE CAUGHT A SECOND-ORDER DEFECT INSIDE ITS OWN FIX: rows are assigned by a running counter and unused slots are deactivated AND COLLAPSED onto the last active row's y — hiding them in place would have left the exact hole the ruling is about, and would have quietly broken the symmetry pin, which reads inactive children too. A fix that passes its own gate by accident is the failure this studio spent the week naming, and this one was found before it could.** **NOT PHOTOGRAPHED AND NOT ORDERED: the moneyline-only panel (one row, 154px) — the mechanism is proven at two row counts and the third is the same formula, so a frame would confirm arithmetic rather than a design. Named so the gap is known.** **THE STATS PHASE IS CLOSED: panel `980 × 480` → `529 × 200` (22.5% of where it began), the scorebug never covered, `GOALS` standing with count rows keyed to the ticket, height derived at adoption, `MATCH STATS` → `COUNTS`, and the unrevealed mark moved from *not in your ticket* to *not yet revealed***

title: THE RAMP RULED — two rungs, and the threshold is 2 rather than 1 because batching SKIPS distance 1
state_raw: **RULED — DD 2026-08-17 batch 109**, answering tv-theater unit 3; detail at `spec-count-theater-2026-08-17.md` §3.6. **THE SHAPE: TWO RUNGS — weighted or quiet. No third treatment and no smooth curve.
body: THE RAMP RULED — two rungs, and the threshold is 2 rather than 1 because batching SKIPS distance 1 | **RULED — DD 2026-08-17 batch 109**, answering tv-theater unit 3; detail at `spec-count-theater-2026-08-17.md` §3.6. **THE SHAPE: TWO RUNGS — weighted or quiet. No third treatment and no smooth curve.** **CORRECTING THIS SEAT'S OWN PHRASING: `T115` says *"a ramp, not a switch"* and that invites a GRADIENT. It should not. The RAMP is in the significance FUNCTION — distance is continuous. The TREATMENT is STEPPED.** From the evidence rather than taste: **the measured failure was NO CONTOUR, and seven slightly-different treatments is seven flavours of one thing — the same flatness with more machinery.** The control's contour was `calm → event → calm`; **three departures from a baseline read where seven departures from nothing did not.** **THE THRESHOLD IS 2, AND IT IS NOT A PREFERENCE — CHECKED AGAINST ALL THREE CORNER LINES THE GENERATOR PRODUCES, on the observed delta pattern: `OVER 8.5` fires ev4 at either threshold; `OVER 10.5` fires ev5 at either; `OVER 9.5` NEVER FIRES at threshold 1 and fires ev4 at threshold 2.** **On a 9.5 line the count steps 8 → 10 and never sits at 9, so a distance-1 approach is SKIPPED and the turn arrives with NO BUILD AT ALL.** **Threshold 2 changes nothing on the other two lines and fixes that one — strictly better, at no cost, across the whole grid.** **§1.5 — THIS IS THE BATCHING HAZARD ONE LEVEL UP AND THIS SEAT NAMED IT THEN FAILED TO APPLY IT:** `grammar-count-markets` §2 records that *a step of 2 can jump the line without ever landing on it* — about the LINE. **The identical property defeats a distance-1 THRESHOLD, and the spec was written without noticing.** **The general form the constant should carry: the approach fires when the leg is WITHIN REACH OF THE NEXT COUNT EVENT — and with batching, "within reach" is not 1.** **THE OTHER RUNGS:** the turn fires on the crossing beat, unchanged; **quiet-once-decided is a STATE check on `RevealedLegOutcome`, NEVER distance arithmetic** (a decided leg is quiet unconditionally, and expressing it as distance invites a negative branch that means nothing); **UNDER takes the same threshold** — its distance is the `LIMIT n` the column already prints — **but NO TURN FIRES ON AN UNDER'S WIN**, which is `T97-am`'s resolved-scene statement and not a beat. **THE CLOCK STAYS OUT OF THE TRIGGER THIS PASS** — tension is a rate and `OVER 9.5` at 8 differs at 70' and 88', but the approach fires once per leg either way, and **adding a second variable before the first has been seen on a single frame is the error this phase has already paid for twice.** Named as the obvious next lever and the reason the constant exists. **WHAT THE CONSTANT MAY VARY: the threshold's VALUE — 2 → 3 is tuning and needs no ruling. WHAT IT MAY NOT VARY WITHOUT A NEW RULING: the two-rung stepped shape, the state-based quiet, the ticket-derived valence, and the exclusion of the clock.** *"A different ramp is one edit"* is true of the NUMBER and not of the SHAPE, **and a knob that can silently change a design is how a ruling gets lost.** **NOT REACHABLE, SO NOT BUILT: concurrent live count legs** — the engine forbids two legs on one matchup and legs sweat sequentially. **The principle if that ever changes: the scene takes the SMALLEST distance across live legs**, which is the hand-over falling out of the same rule. | `[M2] docs/design/spec-count-theater-2026-08-17.md` §3.6

That is the behaviour and it is recorded as such.** **Quieting the corners arm removes ~5.5s (~12.5%), and it is PROBABLY RIGHT: the corners arm ran 41.42s against the control's 35.40s — a 6.02s gap on the same measure — so quieting CONVERGES DURATION ON THE ARM THAT WORKS, closing that gap to ~0.5–0.9s.** The time comes entirely out of the five quieted events (~1.1s each); **the two weighted beats keep their room by construction.** **Length without contour was the complaint, so removing length that carried nothing is removing dead weight, not content.** **ONE CARE SO THE FIGURE IS NOT QUOTED WRONG — TWO DIFFERENT MEASURES ARE IN CIRCULATION: the 12.5% is against the probe's 44.42 SIM-SECONDS; the control comparison is against the read's 41.42/35.40 SWEEP-DURATION table. The convergence holds on either, but the percentage and the comparison are NOT on the same baseline and must not be combined in one sentence.** **THE THREAT THIS CREATES, AND THE FIX: a 12.5% shorter sweat RE-TILES THE WINDOWS** — `deadairNN` fires on 2.5 sim-seconds elapsing since the last window of any kind, **so the after-set will not carry the same window count as the before-set, and the pairing the spec's §8 asks for would be comparing sets with different spines.** **RULED: THE READ ANCHORS ON THE SEVEN COUNT EVENTS — never on windows, frames or time.** The events are pinned by the seed and the pre-planned batch schedule and **do not move**; windows, frame counts and duration all shift and none of them is the spine. **READ CRITERIA, IN PRIORITY ORDER: (1) THE COUNT STILL REACHES 12** — §4's binding and **the only CORRECTNESS check here; if the after-set's final total is short of the before-set's, a quiet corner was consumed without being committed and the fix has shipped a counting bug. THE LAST WORD GOES FIRST.** **AND EVERY AUTHORED COMPACT FORM FOR THE NINE KINDS PUTS THE MARKET'S IDENTIFYING NOUN LAST** — `{CLUB} UNDER 4.5 CORNERS`, `{CLUB} UNDER 1.5 GOALS`, `{CLUB} UNDER 1.5 CARDS`, `{CLUB} OR DRAW`. **The first token truncation removes is the one that says WHICH MARKET THIS IS.** **THIS BREAKS THE PREMISE THE SLOT WAS BUILT ON, and the premise is written in the layout's own canon comment at `:5250` — *"Canon drops the market eyebrow here rather than shrinking it, BECAUSE EVERY AUTHORED STATEMENT ALREADY NAMES ITS OWN MARKET."* The eyebrow was spent on that guarantee. body: The bust frame is SHOOTABLE — and *not a cash-out* turns out to be NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT | **CONDITIONS ADDED, CRITERIA UNCHANGED — DD 2026-08-20 batch 152, written before the frames exist. `T149-am` states the three criteria *"stand exactly as written"* and they still do; nothing here re-authors them.** **FIRST, THE CHECK THAT SHOULD HAVE COME FIRST TWICE BEFORE AND DID THIS TIME (`C59`): THE MECHANISM IS BUILT. `TvSweatScreen.cs:3091-3092` reads `Strike.enabled = _cashOutPreview OR ticketSettled`, with `settledDead` requiring `_ticket.State == TicketState.Lost` AND `revealedLoss` (`:2966-2968`), and the commit's own comment says the leg *"stays struck once the ticket actually settles, BY CASH-OUT OR BY BUST"* (`11e4ad7`, 2026-08-19 23:16). **THIS IS THEREFORE NOT `T148-vf`'s CASE** — that criterion could not be asked at any exposure because the rung did not exist. This one can.** **SECOND, THE DOCK SURVEY, NEGATIVE AND WORTH THE RECORD: 77 image docks scanned; ONE TV candidate carries a genuine lost leg — `drawn-ending-t129-2026-08-19/arm1`, scene003, `grammar-LegFinalLost`. IT FAILS TWICE. (a) ITS FRAMES PREDATE THE MECHANISM BY THREE HOURS (written 20:12; `11e4ad7` at 23:16), and `frame149` read at this seat confirms the pre-remedy state on its face — the footer still says `RISK $25` and `PAYS $58` on a ticket that paid nothing, which is `T121`'s DEFECT rather than its fix. (b) **AND IT WOULD HAVE FAILED ANYWAY, BECAUSE THE TICKET HAS ONE LEG.** The set's own README names arm 2 as *"the only two-leg ticket in the set"*, and `frame149` shows `MIDDLEMEN ML +132 L` with `LEG 1 — DEAD` and NOTHING BENEATH IT.** **THAT SECOND HALF IS THE FINDING AND IT SHARPENS THE PIN. `T149-am` pinned the case to a bust on the ground that a cash-out has no lost leg to confuse the struck ones with. TRUE, AND INCOMPLETE: **A BUST WITH NOTHING AFTER THE LOSER IS EXACTLY AS UNTESTABLE AS A CASH-OUT** — the struck rows are the legs BEHIND the loser, and a one-leg ticket has none. *Not a cash-out* is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and no ruling in this thread said so until now.** **FIVE BINDING CONDITIONS, in the pre-commitment: (1) at least two legs AND THE LOSER IS NOT THE LAST; (2) the loss is REVEALED in the frame, not merely settled in the engine — a burst opened at the bust will contain pre-reveal frames and those are not defects; (3) `C55` — the lost row and at least one struck row IN ONE FRAME, both legible, because the comparison IS the criterion and two frames cannot make it; (4) the chrome row and footer in frame, reading `STAKE` and `RETURNED $0` — if it still reads `RISK`/`PAYS` the settled branch did not run and the frame is not of this subject (`T133-am2`, restated); (5) forcing disclosed in the filename (`S3`).** **A RECIPE OFFERED, NOT IMPOSED — the lane owns the route, and this exists so the window is not spent searching: `GOALLESS-5` ALREADY SUPPLIES BOTH HALVES ON FRAMES THAT EXIST — a `DRAW` leg WINS on that seed (`DRAW +243 W`) and a team-backer leg LOSES on it (`MIDDLEMEN ML +132 L`), and the footer dock's own `S1` ticket carried THREE legs on the same seed. A ticket of MIDDLEMEN ML then DRAW then DRAW busts on leg 1 with two unplayed legs behind it, which is criterion (2)'s state on the seed and matchup already in use** | batch 152
